# Overview

This script:

1)  combines fish data from local/regional, state and federal sources

2)  checks and resolves taxonomic IDs for fish taxa

3)  creates a relative abundance dataset.


# Load in fish data

Fish data was compiled from:

1)  Twin Cities local water management organizations

2)  Minnesota Pollution Control Agency (MPCA, state level)

3)  USGS/USEPA (via finsyncR).

Twin Cities Fish Data was processed and compiled in `module_data_processing_TCMetro.Rmd` and `module_compiling_TC_biodata.Rmd`. Twin Cities data is from the following agencies:

- Riley Purgatory (Twin Cities Metro)

- Carver County (Twin Cities Metro)

- Three Rivers Park District (Twin Cities Metro)

MPCA data was processed and compiled in `module_data_processing_TCMetro.Rmd`

USGS/EPA data was compiled using finsyncR (Mahon et al., 2024) in `module_data_processing_finsyncR.Rmd`

Note that all data are raw counts.

# Clean up data to match across datasets

Resolve taxonomic IDS:

-throw out hybrids

-throw out coarser than species IDs

-for USGS/EPA, if contains ".x." list as hybrid with genus name

For MPCA, how many records are genus only (so species ID)

```{r}

(mpca |> filter(is.na(Species)) |> nrow())/nrow(mpca) #.5% of records are genus only ID - can exclude

mpca2<-mpca |> filter(!is.na(Species)) |> 
  mutate(Date=as.Date(Collection_Date, format="%Y-%m-%d")) |> 
  dplyr::select(-c(Collection_Date))

#Check for duplicates
mpca2 |> janitor::get_dupes()

```

For USGS/USEPA, format columns to match MPCA dataset

```{r}


#Cleaner USGS/USEPA data:
nat2<-nat%>% 
  mutate(Date=as.Date(CollectionDate, format="%Y-%m-%d")) %>% #format date
  dplyr::rename(Original_ID=SiteNumber, Year=CollectionYear, FullScientificName=Name, Latitude=Latitude_dd, Longitude=Longitude_dd, GearType=SampleMethod) %>% #format column names
  mutate(replicate=1) %>%  #add replicate column (no site/date replicates in USGS/EPA dataset)
  dplyr::select(Original_ID, Date, Year, Agency, FullScientificName, Number, Latitude, Longitude, replicate, GearType, COMID) |> 
#remove erroneous duplicates noted above  
  distinct() |> 
  mutate(
    FullScientificName = if_else(
      str_detect(FullScientificName, fixed(".x.")),
      str_replace(FullScientificName, "\\..*", " hybrid"),
      FullScientificName)) |>  #replace any hybrid with "hybrid"
  mutate(FullScientificName = str_replace_all(FullScientificName, "\\.", " ")) |> #format scientific name to match MPCA data
  mutate(Genus = str_extract(FullScientificName, "^[^ ]+")) |>  #Extract genus name
  mutate(Species = str_extract(FullScientificName, "(?<= )[^ ]+")) |> 
  filter(Number>0) #remove 0 counts

head(nat2)

levels(factor(mpca2$FullScientificName))
levels(factor(nat2$FullScientificName))

#Check names that don't match across datasets
#find names in col A that are not in col B
setdiff(mpca2$FullScientificName, nat2$FullScientificName)

setdiff(nat2$FullScientificName,mpca2$FullScientificName) #mpca dataset much more extensive - many more species 

#check duplicates for national data
nat2 |> janitor::get_dupes() #no duplicates

```

For Twin Cities metro data, format to match columns and species designations

```{r}


#target columns:
names(mpca2)

#Make a species look up table from mpca data
taxonomy<-mpca2 |> dplyr::select(Genus, Species, FullScientificName, CommonName, tsn) |> distinct()

#TC data
names(TC.fish)

#ID fish names that aren't in MPCA data

TC.fish |> 
  filter(!CommonName %in% mpca2$CommonName) |> dplyr::select(CommonName) |> distinct()

#View(TC.fish |> filter(CommonName=="na goldfish"))

#Check names used in MPCA dataset
levels(factor(mpca2$CommonName))

#define replacement names for some species to match mpca dataset

replacements<-c(
  "na goldfish" = "goldfish", 
  "na walleye" = "walleye", 
  "na logperch" = "logperch", 
  "na bowfin" = "bowfin", 
  "na drum" = "freshwater drum", 
  "bluegill sunfish" = "bluegill", 
  "pumpkinseed sunfish" = "pumpkinseed", 
  "pumkinseed sunfish" = "pumpkinseed", 
  "northern fathead minnow" = "fathead minnow", 
  "iowa darter" = "Iowa darter")

#format TC fish data and address fish names
TC.fish2<-TC.fish |> 
  rename(Number=Count) |> 
  mutate(CommonName=tolower(CommonName)) |> 
   #format species names to match mpca
  mutate(CommonName = str_replace_all(CommonName, replacements)) |> 
  left_join(taxonomy, by="CommonName") |> 
  dplyr::select(Original_ID, Year, Agency, Genus, Species, FullScientificName, CommonName, tsn, Number, Latitude, Longitude,GearType, Date) |> 
  #remove fish with no or ambiguous ID
  filter(!CommonName=="unknown") |> filter(!is.na(CommonName)) |> 
  filter(!CommonName=="bullhead") |>filter(!CommonName=="sucker") |> filter(!CommonName=="unknown shiner") |> 
  mutate(Date=as.Date(Date))
  

#Check for fish names that didn't have match with mpca data
TC.fish2 |> filter(is.na(Genus)) |> dplyr::select(CommonName) |> distinct()



#View(TC.fish2)


```

```{r}
  mutate(CommonName = Name_filled) |> 
  select(-Name_filled)

nrow(all.fish)
nrow(all.fish2)

missing.lookup

  mutate(CommonName=str_to_sentence(CommonName)) |> #capitalize all common names

  filter(!is.na(Number))
```

# Calculate Relative Abundance

Deal with small inaccuracies in coordinate locations for the same sites by rounding coordinates to same number of digits, and only selecting one set of coordinates for slightly different measures of the same site

```{r}

#Sum count by site/date
names(all.fish.ALL)


all.fish4<-all.fish.ALL |>
  group_by(Original_ID, Latitude, Longitude, Date) |> 
  mutate(TotalCount=sum(Number)) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  mutate(Relative_Abund=Number/TotalCount)

#View(all.fish4)

#save to file
#exclude tsn and COMID for now (may want back later)
write_xlsx(all.fish4 |> dplyr::select(-c(tsn, COMID)), paste0(taxa.dir, "/Fish_relative_abundance.xlsx"))
```
